REPUTATION._note: B4: company Reputation gains (all modes, player titles only, contract jobs ignored). Each level is awarded once per title when its success multiple >= multiple. Success multiple (R1, save v38) = (lifetime receipts - sales costs after launch) / cost up to launch; older titles keep receipts / direct cost. Multiples retuned 3/6/8 -> 6/12/16 with R1 so roughly 10% of titles are Hits, 3% Smashes and under 1% Legendary. Legendary also needs quality or critic score >= minScore. Studio milestones give +1 once each. Reputation cap comes from tuning_engine recognizeCreativeAwards__002.

IPO._note: R7: IPO sized from company value. Public holders own FLOAT of the company after listing; raise = expected valuation x FLOAT/(1-FLOAT). Fee = max(MIN_FEE, raise x FEE_RATE). Public-market money tops up the investor pool by the raise (pool conservation unchanged). Proceeds are paid-in equity, never revenue.

BOARD._note: B1: Board Reputation meter (0-100). Starts at START when the studio incorporates. Yearly review at the first week of each year: target = profit > 0 and revenue >= last year x TARGET_REVENUE_GROWTH. Release effects count only for titles released after incorporation; contract jobs are ignored. A Hit = success multiple >= HIT_MULTIPLE; a Flop = success multiple < FLOP_FRACTION once the title is FLOP_AGE_WEEKS old (success multiple: see REPUTATION note; R1 raised HIT_MULTIPLE 3 -> 6).
BOARD._noteB2: B2: Standard blocks a spend (greenlight total budget, loan, credit line, acquisition, new subsidiary) only if it is above BLOCK_SPEND_SHARE of company value AND Board Reputation is below BLOCK_BELOW. Override cost = round(OVERRIDE_BASE + OVERRIDE_SCALE x spend / company value); refused if it would leave Board Reputation under FLOOR (the block stands). An override is good for PERMIT_WEEKS weeks for that one spend. Below PRESSURE_BELOW at the yearly review the board sends a pressure card: goodwill dividend (PRESSURE_DIVIDEND_FRACTION of lifetime profit, +PRESSURE_DIVIDEND_BONUS) or promise results (next target worth +/-PROMISE_TARGET).

INBOX._note: D3: yearlyCards = max Inbox decision cards per game year (null = no limit). lowPriorityCards = low-priority items only get a card while fewer than this many cards were shown this year. autoDisputes = client delivery disputes are settled automatically (paid rework if affordable, else neutral arbitration).

TABS5._note: D6: Simple and Standard show these 5 tabs instead of the left menu. views = screens inside the tab (first visible one opens by default); a view hidden by HIDE.nav is skipped. Very Complex keeps the left menu.

ADVANCE_TO_DECISION._note: D4: maxWeeks = safety cap for the Advance to next decision button (stops after this many weeks even if no decision card opened). D7: perMode overrides it per depth mode.

PACE_RULES._note: D7 pace levers. releaseCards = a 'Released' card when a player project finishes. allPostmortems = a release report card for every original release, not only major ones (low priority). cashWarningWeeks = a paused (furloughed) studio gets at most one cash warning per this many weeks (null = no limit). mergeCashWeeks = otherwise the low-cash and cash-stress warnings merge within this many weeks.

PACE._note: D7: spec pace targets = decisions per game year (min/max; null = uncapped). robot = how the D7 scripted test player plays each mode (greenlights and client jobs per year). Used by tests only.

PRIORITY._note: Inbox item key prefixes. urgent = always shown as a card. low = shown only under lowPriorityCards. Anything else is normal priority.

HIDE._note: D5: panels whose heading starts with a listed text are not drawn in that mode. simple = standard list + simpleExtra. veryComplex hides nothing. nav = left-menu views hidden per mode (a hidden view falls back to the Overview).

FORMAT_POOLS._note: R2: book spending is split into print, digital and audio buyers. shares lists [world year, share] points for digital and audio (straight lines between points, flat after the last); print gets the rest. A format listed in reach sells only to those buyer groups; formats not listed (Novel, Nonfiction, Comic / Manga) are full releases that reach every group. Total book spending is unchanged.

RECEPTION._note: R1: release reception roll. Each original title (player and AI, not contract jobs) rolls once at release in the listed modes. The roll comes from the world seed and the project id, so it does not use or shift the game's main random stream. Quality moves the roll: shift = clamp((quality - QUALITY_PIVOT) x QUALITY_SHIFT, -MAX_SHIFT, MAX_SHIFT); the level is picked from the cumulative odds at roll + shift. mult multiplies the title's demand weight for its whole life and legs stretches (or shortens) how slowly its sales fade; sales still come out of the same capped regional wallet.
RECEPTION._noteSpread: SPREAD softens (below 1) or sharpens (above 1) the reception effect per sector: the used multiplier is mult^SPREAD and legs^SPREAD.

GENRE_FATIGUE._note: R4: same-genre, same-medium releases sold in a region over the last windowWeeks lower that genre's demand there. Each release counts (1 - age/windowWeeks); background firms count backgroundWeight. Pressure above free[sector] cuts demand by perPoint each, never below floor. Worked out from release history: no save field, no RNG.
